messages:
natalie: quick sync  re: RBAC scoping between org vs project. want to lock down the enforcement model before we write the migration tool.
sam: yea, we need a clear rule set. current state: api keys carry project-id or org-id but enforcement is fuzzy.
lee: proposal: canonicalize three scopes: org-admin, project-admin, service-role. enforcement happens on the data-plane (service) and is backed by authz lookup at the edge.
tom: data-plane checks for every request? worried about latency if we call central auth for each token.
natalie: design: tokens contain a scope claim (org:org-123 | proj:proj-abc | svc:svc-xyz). services do local checks for scope containment and optional role assertions. edge / auth-proxy handles mapping and can optionally offload heavy RBAC evaluation.
sam: how to handle cross-project ops like "move model" or "list keys"? these are org-level but callable by project-admins if granted.
lee: add a policy layer: explicit allowlist rules of the form: {principal_scope, target_scope, actions}. default deny. ex: "proj:proj-abc -> org:org-123 : [artifact:list]"
tom: ok. what's the plan for long-lived API keys? rotation + revocation?
natalie: long-lived keys remain but with reduced privileges. privileged actions (billing, tenant-changes) require 2-step: (1) key must have admin bit, (2) client must use an ephemeral MFA-backed assertion (breakglass for operators).
sam: breakglass tokens should be auditable and short-lived. prefer 15m max. also require an audit reason and link to ticket.
lee: agree. propose audit record format: ``{action, principal, target_scope, reason, ticket, trace_id}``. infra-bot: note -> we will surface trace_id in logs automatically. :robot_face: 
tom: migration: how do we transition existing customers who rely on key propagation across projects?
natalie: migration steps: (a) detect propagation patterns, (b) auto-generate least-privilege service-roles for common flows, (c) provide opt-in enforcement via feature-flagged rollout, (d) enforce by default after 90 days. give customers a migration report.
sam: we should ship a CLI that scans usage and suggests role bindings. also a staged enforcement mode: monitor-only, warn, block.
lee: implementation note: for Dedicated/private, provide a policy-engine plugin so customers can run evaluation locally. token introspection endpoint optional.
tom: what about UI? how do admins see effective permissions?
natalie: UI: effective-permissions view per principal with expand-to-see-polices. also surface risky bindings (org-admins that are service-roles).
sam: error surface: when blocked, return structured error JSON with code ERR_SCOPE_VIOLATION and keys: allowed_scopes, required_action, doc_link. customers can programmatically react.
lee: SDKs: add helper: Auth.checkEffective(principal, action, target) -> {allowed, why}. also cache decisions for 10s.
natalie: ops: add audit retention SLA for 1y for enterprise customers. low-tier default 90d.
natalie: next steps: i'll draft a short RFC with the policy schema + migration timeline. please comment on the allowlist sample and audit fields.
infra-bot: deploy-plan hint -> include a canary in staging + a forced rollback window. will attach a template. :wrench:
